title: Golden History Museum

services.name: Programs At Your School
services.desc: Bring the museum to your classroom with one of our outreach programs facilitated by a museum educator. During this facilitated 90-minute game led by a museum educator, students are divided into historic cultural communities and must make decisions that help their individual progress in the game while taking their group’s needs into consideration. Communities include the Núuchiu (Ute), Tsistsistas (Cheyenne) and Hinono’ei (Arapaho), and Hispano. We establish short and long-term goals, complete trading rounds, cover economics, geography, and history with a real emphasis on building empathy. This program concludes with a contemporary look at the communities discussed throughout the game.

services.name: This exhibit
services.desc: The exhibits at Golden History Museum include versatile programming spaces, a hands-on gallery for families with young children, and dynamic displays that highlight the City’s collection of 16,000 historic objects. Discover your own favorite artifacts in-person and then continue your learning journey at home or in your local coffee shop using our extensive online collection. Learn about Clear Creek’s cultural, industrial, natural, and recreational history. Exhibit made possible in part by Golden Civic Foundation and Molson Coors Beverage Company. services.name: Field Trips
services.desc: Use our walking tour to learn about Golden’s history in 16 fun stops. Start at the Golden Visitors Center, at 1010 Washington Ave, Golden, CO 80401. Navigate using your smartphone and the customized Google map below. Click the photographs to connect with the Museum’s Online Collection and learn more along the walking tour through historic images. Lured not by the riches to be made from mining the hills, but from “mining the miners,” the Boston Company set up the first mercantile in Golden in 1859. services.name: Summer Camp
services.desc: Join us for six weeks of after school club as we explore our Teaching Garden at Golden History Park. Each week, your budding gardener and chef (ages 6 to 11) will observe how our garden changes, explore the fall harvest, and cook up a tasty treat in our historic Pearce Cabin. Wednesdays from 4 - 6 p.m. starting September 16. Club dates include September 16, 23, 30, October 7, 14, 21. Gardener journals, plant identification and care, kitchen safety and cooking skills. Food activities will touch on a variety of fruits, vegetables, and baked goods. Activities will vary based on student interests and garden produce. Parents will receive a full food and ingredient list at the start of club.
